proof:
# Reflected halfspace discrepancy is exactly the two-layer depth loss

Let A,C be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in R^d with volumes 0<a<=b. At bases -1 and 1 let mu be the sum of their ordinary volume measures. Its real-middle depth is evaluated at (0,y), with y allowed to move in R^d. Define the UNNORMALIZED halfspace discrepancy

    Delta(A,C')=sup_H ||A intersect H|-|C' intersect H||,

where H ranges over all ordinary affine halfspaces in R^d. The use of unnormalized volumes is essential when a!=b.

## 1. Exact identity, including unequal volumes

For every y in R^d,

    depth_mu(0,y)=b-Delta(A,2y-C).                        (1)

Write a nonvertical cap through (0,y) as u.x+tz>=u.y, with |u|=1. Put s=u.y+t. Its A trace is H={u.x>=s}, and its C trace is {u.x>=2u.y-s}. Reflection in y converts the latter into the complement of H on C'=2y-C, up to a hyperplane of zero d-volume. Consequently its actual mass is

    b+|A intersect H|-|C' intersect H|.                 (2)

Conversely every ordinary H is obtained by a finite t, so the nonvertical infimum is b-D, where

    D=sup_H(|C' intersect H|-|A intersect H|).

Set T=b-a>=0. Complementary halfspaces exchange each signed discrepancy v with T-v, because their boundaries have zero volume. Also an entire-support halfspace gives discrepancy T, so D>=T. If a discrepancy is negative, its absolute value is at most D-T<=D by the complement relation. Thus D equals the absolute discrepancy Delta. Vertical caps have masses a or b; since Delta>=b-a, the right side of (1) is at most a, so they do not reduce the infimum. A containing cap can be moved to pass through (0,y) while decreasing its mass. This proves (1) for all closed caps.

## 2. Actual optimization and convex level sets

The discrepancy-minimizing translations are exactly the deepest real-middle points:

    max_y depth_mu(0,y)=b-min_y Delta(A,2y-C).            (3)

Both extrema are attained. Indeed the cap function in (2) changes by at most 2L_C|h| when y is replaced by y+h, where L_C is a uniform bound on all (d-1)-dimensional sections of C. Hence Delta is globally Lipschitz with that bound. One may take L_C=omega_(d-1)R^(d-1) if C lies in a ball of radius R; for d=1 use L_C=1.

Let D_0=(A+C)/2. Outside or on the boundary of D_0 a separating/supporting cap takes zero endpoint volume, so the real-middle depth is zero and Delta=b. At the midpoint of any two ordinary interior points of A and C, every cap through that midpoint contains at least one of those endpoint points. Its mass is therefore at least the smaller of their positive own depths. Thus the maximal middle depth is positive, and a discrepancy minimum is attained in int(D_0) by continuity and compactness.

For every beta>0, the set

    {y:Delta(A,2y-C)<=b-beta}

is a compact convex set: by (1) it is a section of an ordinary halfspace-depth superlevel set of the fixed two-layer measure. This can also be seen directly as the intersection of the open-cap exclusions that define depth>=beta. No claim of strict convexity or uniqueness is made. In particular convexity of these level sets supplies no numerical Gamma_d estimate.

## 3. Two exact comparison bounds

Let J(y)=|A intersect (2y-C)|. Every paired cap contains at least J(y): its two pieces on that intersection are complementary under reflection. Equivalently,

    Delta(A,2y-C)<=b-J(y),
    depth_mu(0,y)>=J(y).                                (4)

If A subset 2y-C, then J(y)=a, and the vertical bound gives the exact value

    depth_mu(0,y)=a.                                    (5)

In fact the converse is also true. If depth_mu(0,y)=a, then Delta=b-a=T. By the complementary-halfspace relation in Section 1, every signed discrepancy |C' intersect H|-|A intersect H| lies in [0,T]. If A were not contained in C', separation of a point of A from C' would give a cap with zero C' volume and positive A volume, contradicting that sign. Consequently

    {y:depth_mu(0,y)=a}
       ={y:2y-A subset C}
       =(1/2)(C erosion (-A)),                          (5a)

where the erosion means {t:t-A subset C}. This is an exact convex median-set theorem, independent of endpoint centroids. Its nonemptiness is a genuine shape condition. For intervals it always holds when a<=b; for equal-volume convex bodies it holds exactly when C is a reflected translate of A. It does not imply that the actual middle source has its deepest point at the same y.

There is also a direct quantitative loss when reflected containment fails. Put C'=2y-C, and for a nonzero u let

    w_A(u)=h_A(u)+h_A(-u),
    e_y(u)=min(1, (h_A(u)-h_C'(u))_+/w_A(u)).

All widths are positive. Then

    depth_mu(0,y)<=a [1-sup_u e_y(u)^d].               (5b)

Indeed, if the support gap is between zero and w_A(u), choose a support point v of A in direction u. The homothetic copy v+e_y(u)(A-v) has volume a e_y(u)^d and lies above the supporting hyperplane u.x=h_C'(u). Its boundary has zero volume, while C' has zero volume above that plane. Thus one signed halfspace discrepancy is at most -a e_y(u)^d, and its complement is at least T+a e_y(u)^d. Equation (1) proves (5b). If the gap is at least w_A(u), that separating cap contains all A up to a null boundary and the same argument gives zero depth. The support-gap-to-width ratio is invariant under a common invertible affine change of continuous coordinates.

These are actual cap bounds, not a claim that the remaining shape loss is controlled by volume alone.

If A,C are centrally symmetric about a common origin, the two-layer middle depth is invariant under y->-y. Its quasiconcavity therefore makes y=0 a maximizer. The common-intersection decomposition proved in `candidate 81c79b42fe3af95e` gives

    max_y depth_mu(0,y)>= (a+|A intersect C|)/2.          (6)

For equal-volume crossed rectangles this is equality, with exact value (1+e/L)V/2. Consequently (3) permits a sharp loss as large as V/2 in the equal-volume planar class, even after optimizing the continuous center. This is the precise obstruction to a universal 2Gamma_2 V gluing budget for the endpoint source alone.

## 4. Retaining one actual middle fiber

Now place the endpoints at -1 and 1 and include an arbitrary compatible middle body B, so (A+C)/2 subset B. For an ordinary halfspace H_{u,s}={u.x>=s}, set

    delta_u(y)=sup_s (|(2y-C) intersect H_(u,s)|
                                 -|A intersect H_(u,s)|).

At a fixed actual middle point y in B, the exact nonvertical cap minimum is

    inf_(|u|=1) [|B intersect {u.x>=u.y}|+b-delta_u(y)].  (7)

The same u must be retained in both terms. The only extra competitors are the vertical caps, of masses |B|+a and |B|+b. In particular (1) yields the legitimate lower bound

    depth_(A,B,C)(0,y)>= f_B(y)+b-Delta(A,2y-C),          (8)

where f_B is ordinary unnormalized through-point depth. The vertical caps also satisfy (8), since f_B(y)<=|B| and b-Delta<=a. Formula (8) uses ONE common point y; it does not separate the maximizations of its terms.

This is an exact, finite-dimensional center-translation invariant for paired layers. It is distinct from asserting that optimized directional laws come from one probability measure, from fixing a centroid, or from discarding the forced Minkowski middle mass. No universal lower bound on the maximum in (8) is asserted.

The stdlib verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_reflected_halfspace_two_layer_identity.py` checks 225 rational unequal-volume moving-center interval cases, including both cap orientations, the exact discrepancy identity and every reflected-containment case. It is only an arithmetic cross-check; the dimension-independent proof is above.
